parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
Alright, shall we start? It’s good to see so many people keen to participate in our Young Explorer program I think that at this meeting we have groups from 12 different high schools. I can promise you that while it’s challenging it’s also going to be a lot of fun.

The Young Explorer program offers some unique opportunities to participants. During the program you’ll be trekking through forests or maybe mountain tracks or perhaps kayaking along the coastline. It can be a tough few days but this part of the program really gives your group an occasion to work as a team. Some kind words and encouragement can go a long way. Whether it’s convincing someone they can walk the last five miles or helping them fit everything back inside their backpack No one’s in charge, it’s all about cooperation and please don’t see it as a race. There are going to be moments when there is disagreement about which way to go or where to camp for the night. But here’s the chance to listen properly to the opinions of others and reach a decision that’s best for everyone It’s an opportunity not many other programs provide.

Later this morning you need to choose a weekend when you can attend some preliminary training. A number of practical subjects will be covered to ensure you get the most out of your four day trek. Now everything you eat and drink you’ll have to take with you. You’ll also have to use a portable stove and the fuel it requires. We’ll make sure you know how to use that safely during the training session. We don’t want you or the food to get burnt or for you to accidentally set light to any trees Training will also include learning how to read a map and use a compass so you can head in the right direction. You’ll also need to know how to put up a tent and where to put it. For example, putting it next to a river or a stream might seem like a good idea but there are plenty of reasons not to.

Okay, there are six tracks on your list and your group can decide which track it wants to take. Each of them are about the same distance but very different in other respects. The first one North face, that’s one of my favourite tracks. It takes you high up into the mountains and the view is stunning. But we’ve just heard that some maintenance work is taking place unfortunately and so people aren’t allowed to use it at the moment. But the other tracks are very interesting too. You’ve got Blue River which I’d thoroughly recommend but you need to keep an eye out when you’re walking that track. It’s either too slip on the rocks when you’re crossing the river and you do have to cross it several times.

Then this Pioneer track which takes you through some native forest. You follow the track for about a day and a half and then it comes to an end at a town called Richmond. It starts up again on the other side of town and the rest of the route is along the coast. You might also consider Edgewater. You get to see some beautiful lakes and bird life. The only thing I’d say though is that it’s very popular and you’ll probably come across a number of other groups out walking on the way. Number five on the list is the Murray track. That one is certainly quite challenging. There are some very steep sections and at some points you’d be walking right next to the cliff edge on a very narrow path. That’s definitely a track where caution needs to be taken. Great views though and last but not least is Lakeside track which as the name suggests takes you along one of our biggest lakes. It has some terrific camping spots but that also means it’s a bit of a tourist attraction and you could well be sharing the track with many other visitors. Anyway it’s up to you which track you decided to...

analyses.content: Speaker: Some kind words and encouragement can go a long way... helping them fit everything back inside their backpack.
C 选项（学习新的一项身体技能）虽然提到了徒步和皮划艇，但重点在于团队合作（work as a team），而非技能习得本身；D 选项（环境问题）未提及。
原文提到善意的言语和鼓励很有帮助，比如帮助队友把东西装回背包，这体现了建立支持性关系。

原文提到必须使用便携式炉具及其燃料，并且会在培训中确保你知道如何安全使用它。

analyses.content: Speaker: Training will also include learning how to read a map and use a compass so you can head in the right direction.
E 选项（用木头建庇护所）是干扰项，原文说的是搭帐篷（put up a tent），而不是用木头建。
培训包括学习如何看地图和使用指南针，以便你能朝着正确的方向前进，即跟随路线。

analyses.content: Speaker: But we’ve just heard that some maintenance work is taking place unfortunately and so people aren’t allowed to use it at the moment.
"People aren’t allowed to use it at the moment" 对应选项 C "closed"。
关于 Northface，原文说不幸的是正在进行维护工作，所以目前不允许人们使用。
关于 Blue River，原文提到过河时岩石上太滑（too slip/slippery），而且需要多次过河，存在安全隐患。
Speaker: It’s either too slip on the rocks when you’re crossing the river and you do have to cross it several times.
"Too slip on the rocks" 对应选项 B "unsafe"。
Speaker: Then this Pioneer track... then it comes to an end at a town called Richmond. It starts up again on the other side of town...
"Comes to an end... starts up again" 对应选项 D "divided into two sections"。
关于 Pioneer，这条路在一个叫 Richmond 的镇子结束（comes to an end），然后从镇子的另一边重新开始（starts up again），分为两段。
Speaker: The only thing I’d say though is that it’s very popular and you’ll probably come across a number of other groups out walking on the way.
"Come across a number of other groups" 对应选项 A "busy"。
关于 Edgewater，原文说它非常受欢迎，你可能会在路上遇到很多其他团体。
Speaker: There are some very steep sections and at some points you’d be walking right next to the cliff edge on a very narrow path.
"Steep sections... next to the cliff edge... caution needs to be taken" 对应选项 B "unsafe"。
关于 Murray，原文提到有非常陡峭的路段，甚至紧邻悬崖边缘行走，必须小心，意味着这地方不安全。
Speaker: ...it’s a bit of a tourist attraction and you could well be sharing the track with many other visitors.
"Sharing the track with many other visitors" 对应选项 A "busy"。
关于 Lakeside，因为它是一个旅游景点，你很可能会与许多其他游客共享这条路。
